key_insight: The paper proposes a two-level framework that ranks EHR-discovered disease trajectories by both semantic novelty and clinical priority, rather than relying on structural support alone.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers focus on the most potentially informative trajectory patterns for retrospective study and hypothesis generation, while avoiding overinterpretation of novelty as clinical causality.
method: Encoded three textual versions of each trajectory motif/node-target pair with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5.
Compared embeddings against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using mean top-20 cosine distance to estimate semantic sparsity/novelty.
Combined novelty with reliability-adjusted priority signals and tested robustness across templates, encoders, taxonomies, and scoring settings.
evidence_signal: In the frozen high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting improved conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points, but broader ranking stability and some downstream associations were mixed.
watch_item: The framework supports literature-relative prioritization, not causal discovery or clinician-adjudicated novelty, so its scores should not be treated as direct clinical guidance.
paper_title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
